name: Great Basin National Park
summary: One of America's least-visited parks — a 13,000-ft peak, ancient bristlecone pines, a marble cave, and some of the darkest skies on the continent.

lodging.name: A Baker, NV inn (or campground)
lodging.blurb: Tiny gateway town at the park's edge.

item.title: Lehman Caves & Wheeler Peak
item.blurb: Tour the ornate Lehman Caves, drive up toward 13,065-ft Wheeler Peak, and walk to the ancient bristlecone pines — the oldest trees on earth.

days.label: Day 385 — Across the Loneliest Road
days.summary: Basin and range, all the way to Death Valley.

commute.scenicNote: West on US-6 through Ely and Tonopah, then south on US-95 — mountain range, empty basin, mountain range, for five hours. There is almost nothing out here, which is the point. Fill the tank in Tonopah.

stopsAlongWay.title: Goldfield
stopsAlongWay.blurb: Nevada's biggest city in 1906 and nearly a ghost town now — the Goldfield Hotel still stands empty on the main street.

stopsAlongWay.title: Rhyolite ghost town
stopsAlongWay.blurb: A bank, a jail, a house built of bottles, and a yard of ghostly plaster sculptures, just outside the park's northern gate.
